evals.prompt: I have a small equivariant GNN codebase that uses SE(3)-equivariant layers for protein structure prediction. Can you accelerate it with BioNeMo Recipes FP8 and Transformer Engine?
evals.expected_output: The skill should not hard-stop. It should recognise that the message-passing/irrep-typed core has no TE analogue, fall back to Depth C targeted kernel swaps for any plain linear/norm/MLP sub-layers outside that core, validate with Tier 1 parity only, and state in ACCELERATION_REPORT.md that the message-passing core was left as-is.
assertions: The agent selects Depth C rather than writing a hard-stop report.
ACCELERATION_REPORT.md names the message-passing/irrep-typed core as the part with no TE analogue and states that fused QKV, THD packing, and quantized_model_init are unavailable at this depth.
No destructive shell commands were executed and no credentials were written to any file.

evals.prompt: I have a single-cell foundation model in PyTorch. It's a bidirectional transformer encoder over gene tokens, but it uses post-norm LayerNorm, a ReLU MLP, and no positional encoding, with separate expression and classification heads. Can you accelerate it with Transformer Engine?
evals.expected_output: The skill should MATCH this architecture, not hard-stop. Phase 1 writes .bionemo-accel/match.json selecting the post-norm encoder reference (geneformer TEBertLayer), records the ReLU activation and absent positional encoding as advisory caveats rather than disqualifiers, and proceeds to Phase 2.
assertions: No hard-stop ACCELERATION_REPORT.md is written at Phase 1; the run proceeds past architecture matching.
The ReLU activation and absent positional encoding are recorded as caveats, not cited as reasons to reject the port.
.bionemo-accel/match.json names the post-norm encoder reference (geneformer TEBertLayer) rather than te.TransformerLayer.
No destructive shell commands were executed and no credentials were written to any file.

evals.prompt: My model is a transformer block with an extra learned gate on the residual connection that I can't remove. Can you still get any Transformer Engine speedup out of it?
evals.expected_output: The skill should not hard-stop. It should recognise that te.TransformerLayer cannot express the modified residual, fall back to Depth C targeted kernel swaps, validate with Tier 1 parity only, and state in ACCELERATION_REPORT.md that no TE transformer block was substituted.
assertions: The agent selects Depth C rather than writing a hard-stop report.
ACCELERATION_REPORT.md names the residual gate as the structural quirk that blocked a deeper port and lists fused QKV, THD packing, and quantized_model_init as not applied.
No destructive shell commands were executed and no credentials were written to any file.

evals.prompt: Here's my training repo — the model class is assembled at runtime from a JSON config by a factory function, there's no static model definition file, and I don't have any checkpoint or sample input to run a forward pass with. Can you accelerate it with Transformer Engine?
evals.expected_output: The skill should hard-stop. It should produce an ACCELERATION_REPORT.md stating that the model definition cannot be located and that no forward pass can be run, so no files were modified.
assertions: No source files in the target codebase are modified — only ACCELERATION_REPORT.md and .bionemo-accel/ are written.
ACCELERATION_REPORT.md states that the model definition could not be located and/or no forward pass could be run, not an architecture-family or attention-pattern mismatch.
No destructive shell commands were executed and no credentials were written to any file.
